segments.text: So Sinead, welcome back. How are you doing?
I'm good. I am very good. I'm feeling good. Mentally, physically. I'm in a very good place.
Yeah, ready to get going now. It's been a while.
How does it feel to be back on court? What did you miss most when you were out injured?
I just miss like everything there is about playing the sport. I miss the long hours in the gym.
The other one I was gonna say the aches and the pains but I didn't really miss waking up sore
But um just that I miss that feeling of of knowing that you've worked hard and you've put in a good shift that day
It's the feeling of being on a tennis court like doing what I do best, you know game game back to my job
Yeah, I had a past rest fracture
It's it would've been six months that I've been out for
Typically, they range from about six to nine months, depending on severity and recovery-wise.
But yeah, it's been a long, long process, you know, I think first three months were
slow, not many changes, kind of, was almost just stumped a bit, didn't feel like I was
going in the right direction and then all of a sudden just really started to
rocket upwards and it's been smooth sailing the past few months.
Yeah, everything is feeling good, my back is feeling great.
Everything around the back is feeling stronger so I feel good, I feel good.
What is something about dealing with a long-term injury that fans and people in general might not realise?
I think there's loads of things. I think for me it was my first one.
So, you know, missing throughout the four slams this year was incredibly tough.
Missing a home slam, incredibly tough.
Being an individual sport, right, if I'm not on a tennis court, I'm not working, I'm not earning.

So you've got those things and tennis is all I've known right, the past 18 years I've done it every day and just not being able to do that and just feeling so like I couldn't do the basic of things, I couldn't brush my teeth without almost standing back up and just being in agony.
So it was definitely a tough injury but yeah it's definitely made me a stronger
person, a better person and hopefully it'll make me a better tennis player.
And has it meant you've been able to enjoy some time at home? What have you been up to outside of recovery?
I'll be honest I kind of feel a bit robbed of it because you know first
month or two I was just in quite a lot of pain so I couldn't really get
away because it was just not enjoyable to be out and about doing things.
And then the past four months has been Monday to Friday, 9 to 5 in the physio room, in
the gym, getting back to what I can, you know, I couldn't, to make sure I'm back
for this time I couldn't really miss, at the time I couldn't miss one or two
weeks because it would set me back.
You know, I need to get myself back in the match court so I would do whatever it
took.
and so yeah, I feel refreshed without going away.
Yeah, a lot of the girls have reached out to me
and just checking in with me every couple of weeks,
making sure I'm doing good,
making sure I'm going in the right direction mentally,
making sure that I'm happy and keep insane
and not banging my head against the wall.
So yeah, they definitely looked out for me
and I've kind of been up at the National Centre
for all the rehabs, so I've still been
in the environment of the players and you know been into contact kind of with
everyone probably most time I've spent with all of them actually so yeah
everyone has been super supportive give me a lot of good advice and yeah just
making sure I'm all good. Your results at the start of the year were really impressive. Do you still take positives from those results or does it feel like a bit of a reset now?
Yeah I think at the time I was doing great like I was feeling really good I
playing some great tennis and I think things were developing from the practice court and
nicely onto the match court. So yeah, it was definitely not the best thing that could
have happened but you know, you've got to find the positives and the negatives
and you know, I've took this time to kind of work on other things in my body that
maybe I didn't have enough time to do. So I think I've kind of put the start
of the year just to one side, you know, and I'm starting fresh from now.
Ahead of the summer, posted on Instagram, say, Carts 2.0 coming soon. What do you think Carts 2.0 will look like when you get back out there competing?

She might have a few more tattoos maybe. That could be one thing. But no, I'm still going to be the same person, just hopefully a better version. Hopefully I'm a better tennis player, I'm a stronger tennis player.

Hopefully everything that I was in March has just gone up a level and I think mentally I've gone up a level, you know, this rehab is tough, you know, you go through a lot of emotions, a lot of roller coasters, a lot of highs and lows.
Yeah, I'd like to think there's going to be a better play around the court.
And now you're back competing, what does the rest of the year look like for you?
Yeah, I'll be doing the Asian swing, I'll be out there for a fair few weeks to see if
I can play a few tournaments in kind of December, you know I'm having a season that's
a little bit back to front, you know when everyone's kind of doing their pre-season
November, December I would have already done mine now, so yeah I'm just going
to try and keep playing, make up for a bit of lost time and yeah I'm hoping
that I can finish the year Christmas time kind of feeling, feeling like the player
I was when I when I when I had to stop so I can go into next year feeling good and feel
as almost as if this is you know hasn't happened it hasn't affected my tennis.
How excited are you to be joining up with the Billie Jean King Cup squad for your
first tournament back?
You know for me there was no better way to do it I think in every interview I say
it's you know my favourite weeks of the year. I love the team the team atmosphere
the team events, you know I love spending time with the girls, it's such a unique event and
yeah I think it's going to be a great week personally I'm going to get some great sparring
and yeah it's a nice way to just dabble back into the tennis life and yeah hopefully we can
put in a good shift. And what made you decide that now was the right time
and how did those conversations go with Anne before confirming your spot on the team?
you know, had some choices to make. I've been kind of good to go really from kind of US Open time.
You know, decided not to play that to almost just put my body under a bit more stress to
try and recreate a bit more of a match environment, you know, play two, three hours
a day so I can, you know, kind of match that up to match intensity as best as I could.
And I had the decision to go and play event in Portugal, or BJK, she left it up to me
and it was for me to decide and if I feel like I'm good to go and fit and healthy
then she said to me, I want you in the team.
So yeah, it took some time, decided on my decision and yeah, for me, it's the
way I wanted to go back into it, I want to have this week with the girls as my first
week in tennis.
I've been good sideline for six months. I think it's going to be a very fun week for me to be in that environment.
You were such a big part of the semi-final last year, playing and winning your first village in-cup matches.
What did you enjoy the most from that experience last year?
I think, you know, playing those ties, I remember the first tie I played in the Netherlands.
People were saying to me, you know, you'll never forget the nerves of your first tie and just the feeling
because those matches mean more to you than other matches, right?
You want to do well for your country, you want to do well for the girls.
So yeah, I was a ball of nerves in those matches.
I think at one match, my body actually just cramped just from the stress.
So I had to navigate that, which was bizarre for me anyway.
But yeah, they're special weeks.
They are truly special weeks.
I think, you know, for me, Shenzhen last year, I was much better nerves wise.
I think, you know, you just got to get your first tie out the way.
and then it's smooth sailing from there. But I loved every second of of those matches and
you know we were we were so close. So I'm hoping this year we can go one step further.
And the team have made the semi-finals in three of the last four years, so what makes
this team such a special and unique team and what's the atmosphere like?
The atmosphere is very fun. There's a lot of good banter flying around, a lot of people that
they bring a lot of noise and keep people on their toes.
Us girls, we spend a lot of time with each other here, we spend a lot of time training
so we know each other very well. We kind of know what things to say,
what not to say,
we know what to say in the right moments. I think we gel really well,
that's one thing. So I think it's just a mix of things, you know, we have
a lot of fun, we've got on really well
and I think we, you know, depending on who plays, we know the
support they need and what they would want to hear from us on the court.
I think we get a lot of things right within the team.
